explain.say: Look around you. How many wheels can you spot? Car, bike, suitcase, even a chair! But long ago there were no wheels at all. Look at the timeline to see how the wheel rolled into our lives.

explain.say: About 4,000 years ago, people made spoked wheels: thin rods instead of a solid disc. They were much lighter, so horse chariots could race fast. Look at the water wheel next: flowing rivers turned wheels to grind grain into flour.

faq.a: About 5,500 years ago, around 3500 BCE. Potter's wheels appeared in Mesopotamia, and wheels on carts appeared soon after in several places.

faq.q: What was the first wheel used for?
faq.a: The earliest known wheels were potter's wheels, used to spin clay into round pots, before wheels were used on carts.
asks: Was the first wheel for carts?

faq.q: What is the oldest wheel ever found?
faq.a: The Ljubljana Marshes Wheel from Slovenia, made of wood about 5,150 years ago. Its axle was found with it.
An axle is the rod through the middle of a wheel. The wheel turns around it, or turns with it, so a cart can roll.
asks: How does a wheel and axle work?

faq.a: Spokes are thin rods that join the middle to the rim. They make a wheel much lighter but still strong, so vehicles can go faster.

facts: The Ljubljana Marshes Wheel, found in Slovenia, is about 5,150 years old, the oldest known wooden wheel with an axle.
John Boyd Dunlop developed a practical air-filled (pneumatic) tyre in 1888.
